$comment: Machine-readable shape of the Constancia data layer. Source of truth for the schema canvas and, later, for generated Pydantic models. Every collection carries user_id; those edges are omitted from diagrams by convention.

collections.name: goals
collections.summary: Narrative is the truth; measurables are a revisable interpretation.

fields.notes[]: { text: string, at: Date, author: "user"|"advisor"|"professional", assessment_id: ObjectId? -> assessments }
fields.created_from: { by: "user"|"advisor"|"professional", reason: string, assessment_ids: ObjectId[] -> assessments, evidence: ObjectId[] -> sessions }

collections.name: assessments
collections.summary: Medical and professional input. Hard constraints outrank goals in agent prompts.

fields.measurements[]: { metric: string, value: float, unit: string }
fields.constraints[]: { text: string, until: date_str?, hard: bool }
fields.source: "user_reported" | "document" | "manual_entry"  // a verbal report is weaker evidence than an uploaded lab report

collections.name: routines
collections.summary: Versioned training plan. User-named days, no load targets.

fields.name: string
fields.created_from: { by: "user"|"advisor", reason: string, evidence: ObjectId[] -> sessions }
fields.days[].key: string  // stable, minted once, never changes
fields.days[].label: string  // display, editable

collections.name: users
collections.summary: Auth, WhatsApp link, timezone. Phone number is the chat credential.

fields.name: string
fields.profile: { timezone: string, units: "metric"|"imperial", daily_spend_cap_usd: float, language: { primary: "en", secondary: "es"?, show_both: bool } }

collections.name: exercise_library
collections.summary: Global catalog of anything you can DO — strength, cardio, sport, mobility, mindfulness. English canonical, Spanish secondary.

fields.name: { en: string, es: string? }  // en is canonical, always present
fields.muscle_groups: string[]  // empty for sport and mindfulness

collections.name: user_exercises
collections.summary: Per-user overlay: aliases and local machine calibration.

fields.aliases[]: { text: string, lang: "en"|"es", hits: int, last_seen: Date, source: "confirmed"|"inferred" }  // max 12, evict lowest hits

collections.name: sessions
collections.summary: strength | cardio | recovery. One collection, discriminated by type.

fields.adherence: { planned: int, completed: int, substituted: int, skipped: int, unplanned: int }?
fields.exercises[].sets[]: { order: int, reps: int?, seconds: int?, load: { value: float, unit: string }?, load_kg: float?, rir: int?, note: string? }
fields.detail: { activity_id: ObjectId -> exercise_library, duration_min: int, distance_km: float?, intensity: "low"|"moderate"|"high" }?  // type != strength

collections.name: daily_metrics
collections.summary: Weight, steps, water, sleep. aggregation decides sum vs. point.

fields.aggregation: "point" | "daily_total"  // daily_total SUMS across the day; point does not

collections.name: messages
collections.summary: Raw inbound, TTL 90 days. Voice notes are transcribed once on arrival; the audio itself never reaches the LLM.

fields.media[]: { key: string, mime: string, duration_s: int?, transcript: string?, transcript_lang: "es"|"en", transcribed_at: Date? }

collections.name: entry_drafts
collections.summary: The completeness gate and the only conversation state.

fields.unresolved[]: { text: string, candidates: [{ exercise_id: ObjectId, score: float }], action: "confirm_or_create" }

collections.name: daily_summaries
collections.summary: Materialized per user per day. Safe to drop and rebuild.

fields.metrics: { body_weight: float?, steps: int?, water_l: float?, sleep_h: float? }
fields.macros: { kcal: float, protein_g: float, carbs_g: float, fat_g: float }

collections.name: model_calls
collections.summary: One cost ledger for every paid external call — LLM and speech-to-text alike, so the per-user spend cap covers both.

fields.audio_seconds: float?  // STT bills by duration, not tokens

collections.name: proposals
collections.summary: An outgoing suggested plan change awaiting the user's answer. Mirrors entry_drafts, which is the state for incoming data.

fields.trigger: { kind: "new_assessment"|"deviation"|"goal_conflict"|"scheduled_review", assessment_id: ObjectId? -> assessments, evidence: ObjectId[] -> sessions }
fields.rationale: string  // why, in the user's language
fields.changes[]: { target: "goal"|"routine"|"diet", target_id: ObjectId, summary: string, patch: object }
fields.outcome_ids: ObjectId[]  // new versions created on accept

collections.name: meal_templates
collections.summary: A named dish you eat repeatedly, with macros already worked out. Always user-scoped — food is personal, so there is no global library.

fields.user_id: ObjectId -> users  // ALWAYS scoped, never global
fields.name: string  // "desayuno clásico"
fields.aliases[]: { text: string, lang: "en"|"es", hits: int, last_seen: Date, source: "confirmed"|"inferred" }  // max 12
fields.description: string  // the user's own words, verbatim
fields.macros: { kcal: float, protein_g: float, carbs_g: float, fat_g: float }
fields.evidence[]: { kind: "nutrition_label"|"recipe"|"plate", extracted: object, media_key: string?, read_at: Date }
fields.created_by: "user" | "promotion"  // named outright, or emerged from repeats

collections.name: meals
collections.summary: One thing eaten. Macros are copied onto it, never read through the template, so correcting a template never rewrites history.

fields.macros: { kcal: float, protein_g: float, carbs_g: float, fat_g: float }  // COPIED, never referenced
fields.photo_key: string?  // short TTL — decoration once the estimate exists

language_policy.note: English is canonical for every resource name — exercises, sports, units. Spanish is a secondary display and matching layer. Users can show both.

media_policy.principle: Voice is the best meal input. Photos build templates. Text logs meals.
rules: A nutrition label or recipe photo is extraction — high accuracy, done once at template creation.
A plate photo is estimation — a guess, and the one that would recur daily.
Never refuse a photo. Make the template path faster instead.
Cache by image hash so a resent or retried photo never re-bills.
Over the daily spend cap, degrade to the nightly Batch API rather than declining.
Keep extracted numbers plus a thumbnail on templates; full-resolution originals are optional.
Plate photos on one-off meals get a short TTL like message media.
Transcribe a voice note once on arrival, store the transcript on the media entry, then treat it as ordinary text — the audio never reaches the LLM.
Pin the transcription language from users.profile.language rather than auto-detecting; mixed Spanish and English breaks detection.
Numbers are what speech-to-text gets wrong, and numbers are what matter. Echo the quantities heard back, not just the computed result.
input_ranking: 2. Voice note — cheap to transcribe, and people say quantities aloud that they would never type. Best quality per unit of effort.
3. Typed text — same pipeline as voice, but shorter and vaguer because typing is work.
4. Plate photo — most expensive, least accurate. Fallback, not default.
Label and recipe photos sit outside this ranking: extraction, not estimation, and they belong at template creation.

precision_policy.principle: Reward precision, never require it. Ask for weights at template creation, not at logging.
rules: A vague meal is logged first, then optionally refined — logging never blocks on a question.
basis records why a number is what it is: weighed beats described beats photo_estimate.
At most one precision nudge per day, so it cannot become an interrogation.

transcription.decision: Hosted API with its own key, not self-hosted whisper.
transcription.component: A dedicated audio agent whose only job is audio -> text.
rules: The audio agent transcribes and stops. It never interprets — once it is text, the existing triage/resolve/draft path handles meaning, so there is only ever one interpretation path to debug.
It may return per-word confidence or alternatives for numbers; the confirmation message highlights the uncertain quantity.
Language is pinned from users.profile.language, never auto-detected.
Every call is logged to model_calls with provider 'stt' and audio_seconds, so transcription counts against the same per-user spend cap as the LLM.
The backend sits behind an adapter like the LLM gateway, so it is swappable without touching the pipeline.
